options.systemMessage:
You are classifying Slack messages sent to a data engineering team channel.

Respond with ONLY one of these exact values — no punctuation, no explanation, nothing else:
AD_HOC_QUERY
PIPELINE_REQUEST
NOT_RELEVANT

Rules:
- AD_HOC_QUERY: someone needs data pulled, a metric checked, or a one-off report run now.
- PIPELINE_REQUEST: the request implies a recurring report, a Jasper report, a dbt model, an Airflow DAG, or any scheduled/automated data delivery.
- NOT_RELEVANT: casual conversation, thank-yous, announcements, or anything unrelated to data work.

You are a senior data engineering assistant with direct access to ClickHouse via MCP tools and dbt Semantic definitions via Postgres. 

You have access to these tools:
- get_all_dbt_semantic_schemas: Returns the complete, official dbt semantic model and metrics definitions (tables, columns, metrics, dimensions, filters).
- run_select_query: Executes a read-only SELECT query. Use this for SELECT queries only. You can use it to preview data ONLY where in doubt of the actual underlying data. Never run DDL or DML.

When the semantic schema identifies the relevant table and columns but does not define how a requested business value is represented, use run_select_query to inspect the actual data before writing the final SQL.

For low-cardinality categorical fields, use a DISTINCT preview with LIMIT 1000.

Example:
SELECT DISTINCT feature
FROM product_events.events
LIMIT 1000

Do NOT call list_tables. The dbt semantic schema tool is the authoritative source for available tables and columns.

Do NOT repeatedly call schema or metadata tools after the relevant table and columns have already been identified.

ALWAYS follow this exact order:
1. Call get_all_dbt_semantic_schemas BEFORE writing any SQL to inspect the official metrics, valid categorical/time dimensions, filters, and exact underlying table strings.
2. Use ONLY column names, table names, metrics, pre-defined semantic filters, and meta.physical_relation values observed in the dbt semantic schema metadata. Never infer or invent how a business feature, event, or property is represented in the data. If the requested feature/event value is not explicitly defined in the semantic metadata, use `run_select_query` tool with a LIMIT 1000 to inspect the relevant low-cardinality columns before writing the final SQL.
3. Use meta.physical_relation as the authoritative physical ClickHouse table when generating SQL.
4. If the request needs tables or metrics outside those defined in the schemas, set outside_scope=true, do NOT write a query, and flag for confirmation.
5. Write the full SQL using real schema/table/column names from step 1. Ensure that your SQL syntax is strictly CLICKHOUSE COMPATIBLE. Multi-statement queries are not allowed.

Special ClickHouse JSON Rules:
- If a semantic definition specifies that a dimension or property is located inside a JSON string column (like `product_events.events.properties`), you MUST use ClickHouse JSON extraction functions (e.g., `JSONExtractString(properties, 'key_name')`) instead of querying it directly.

Respond ONLY in this JSON format — no prose, no markdown fences:
{
  "summary": "one sentence summary of the request",
  "tables_needed": ["schema.table1", "schema.table2"],
  "outside_scope": false,
  "proposed_query": "SELECT ...",
  "output_format": "table | csv | summary",
  "confidence": "high | medium | low",
  "note": "optional — include ONLY when outside_scope is true or the schemas are empty. Explain what is missing, what you checked, and what clarification you need from the requester. This field should default to JUST an empty string when you have a valid query."
}

You are a senior data engineering assistant planning a data pipeline request.

The request has already been classified as a PIPELINE_REQUEST (recurring report, Jasper report, dbt model, or Airflow DAG).

Your job:
1. Summarise what is being asked in one sentence.
2. Identify the likely ClickHouse tables needed (from ONLY THE FOLLOWING schemas: analytics, product_events, user_metrics).
3. Identify the pipeline type: Jasper Report | dbt Model | Airflow DAG | Other.
4. Write the foundational SQL query that would power it.
5. Note any scheduling or delivery requirements mentioned.

Respond ONLY in this JSON format — no prose, no markdown fences:
{
  "summary": "one sentence summary",
  "pipeline_type": "Jasper Report | dbt Model | Airflow DAG | Other",
  "tables_needed": ["schema.table1", "schema.table2"],
  "outside_scope": false,
  "proposed_query": "SELECT ...",
  "scheduling_notes": "e.g. daily at 8am, on-demand, etc.",
  "confidence": "high | medium | low"
}

parameters.content:
## Response Parsing Via Webhooks
## **How this Works:** _Messages get posted to Slack, With action buttons that have resume URLs. Clicking on any of the action buttons (within the wait Window) triggers this webhook and parses the routes differently._

## Data Request Handling
## **How this Works:** _Messages Posted to Slack for data engineering/analytics requests via a dedicated #data-requests are classified as Adhoc or New Pipeline/Report Deployment. Adhoc Requests are handled by AI with a human in the Loop. and answers get sent back to the requester._

## _In case of Declined AI suggestions or a more detailed task that requires more work. A Jira ticket is opened_

parameters.toolDescription: Returns the official dbt semantic model definitions, including metrics, dimensions, columns, source tables, and aggregation logic. Use this before writing SQL.

assignments.name: analytics.yml
assignments.value: version: 2  models:   - name: fct_conversions     meta:       physical_relation: analytics.conversions     description: >       User conversion events including signups, upgrades, and purchases.      semantic_model:       enabled: true      agg_time_dimension: event_time      columns:        - name: user_id         description: User associated with the conversion.         entity:           name: user           type: foreign        - name: event_date         description: Calendar date of the conversion.         granularity: day         dimension:           type: time        - name: event_time         description: Timestamp when the conversion occurred.         granularity: second         dimension:           type: time        - name: conversion_type         description: Type of conversion event.         dimension:           type: categorical        - name: plan         description: Product plan associated with the conversion.         dimension:           type: categorical        - name: campaign_id         description: Marketing campaign associated with the conversion.         dimension:           type: categorical      metrics:        - name: conversions         description: Total conversion events.         type: simple         agg: count         expr: 1        - name: converted_users         description: Distinct users with a conversion event.         type: simple         agg: count_distinct         expr: user_id        - name: conversion_revenue_usd         description: Total revenue recorded from conversion events in USD.         type: simple         agg: sum         expr: revenue_usd    - name: fct_page_views     meta:       physical_relation: analytics.page_views     description: >       Website page-view events. One row represents one page view by a user       within a session.      semantic_model:       enabled: true      agg_time_dimension: event_time      columns:        - name: user_id         description: Unique identifier for the user who viewed the page.         entity:           name: user           type: foreign        - name: session_id         description: Unique identifier for the browsing session.         entity:           name: session           type: primary        - name: event_date         description: Calendar date of the page view.         granularity: day         dimension:           type: time        - name: event_time         description: Timestamp when the page view occurred.         granularity: second         dimension:           type: time        - name: page_url         description: Page viewed.         dimension:           type: categorical        - name: referrer         description: Referrer that led to the page view.         dimension:           type: categorical        - name: device_type         description: Device category used for the page view.         dimension:           type: categorical        - name: country         description: Country associated with the page view.         dimension:           type: categorical      metrics:        - name: page_views         description: Total number of page views.         type: simple         agg: count         expr: 1        - name: unique_page_view_users         description: Number of distinct users who viewed pages.         type: simple         agg: count_distinct         expr: user_id        - name: total_time_on_pages_seconds         description: Total recorded page-view duration in seconds.         type: simple         agg: sum         expr: duration_seconds        - name: average_page_view_duration_seconds         description: Average recorded duration of a page view.         type: simple         agg: average         expr: duration_seconds

assignments.name: product_events.yml
assignments.value: version: 2  models:   - name: fct_product_events     meta:       physical_relation: product_events.events     description: >       Product interaction events. One row represents one product event       performed by a user.      semantic_model:       enabled: true      agg_time_dimension: event_time      columns:        - name: user_id         description: User who generated the product event.         entity:           name: user           type: foreign        - name: session_id         description: Session in which the product event occurred.         entity:           name: session           type: foreign        - name: event_date         description: Calendar date of the event.         granularity: day         dimension:           type: time        - name: event_time         description: Timestamp when the event occurred.         granularity: second         dimension:           type: time        - name: event_name         description: Name of the product event.         dimension:           type: categorical        - name: feature         description: Product feature associated with the event.         dimension:           type: categorical      metrics:        - name: product_events         description: Total number of product events.         type: simple         agg: count         expr: 1        - name: active_product_users         description: Distinct users who generated at least one product event.         type: simple         agg: count_distinct         expr: user_id        - name: active_product_sessions         description: Distinct sessions containing product events.         type: simple         agg: count_distinct         expr: session_id    - name: fct_feature_usage_daily     meta:       physical_relation: product_events.feature_usage_daily     description: >       Daily pre-aggregated product feature usage statistics.      semantic_model:       enabled: true      agg_time_dimension: event_date      columns:        - name: event_date         description: Date of the feature usage aggregation.         granularity: day         dimension:           type: time        - name: feature         description: Product feature being measured.         dimension:           type: categorical      metrics:        - name: feature_unique_users         description: >           Sum of daily unique users using a feature. This is additive across           features but may overcount users across multiple days.         type: simple         agg: sum         expr: unique_users        - name: feature_usage_events         description: Total recorded feature events.         type: simple         agg: sum         expr: total_events

assignments.name: user_metrics.yml
assignments.value: version: 2  models:   - name: dim_users     meta:       physical_relation: user_metrics.users     description: >       User dimension containing user attributes, signup information,       subscription plan, geography, and current active status.      semantic_model:       enabled: true      agg_time_dimension: signup_date      columns:        - name: user_id         description: Unique identifier for a user.         entity:           name: user           type: primary        - name: signup_date         description: Date the user signed up.         granularity: day         dimension:           type: time        - name: plan         description: Current subscription plan for the user.         dimension:           type: categorical        - name: country         description: Country associated with the user.         dimension:           type: categorical        - name: is_active         description: Whether the user is currently active.         dimension:           type: categorical      metrics:        - name: users         description: Total users.         type: simple         agg: count_distinct         expr: user_id        - name: active_users         description: Users currently marked as active.         type: simple         agg: count_distinct         expr: case when is_active = 1 then user_id end        - name: inactive_users         description: Users currently marked as inactive.         type: simple         agg: count_distinct         expr: case when is_active = 0 then user_id end    - name: fct_daily_signups     meta:       physical_relation: user_metrics.daily_signups     description: >       Daily pre-aggregated signup and signup-related revenue metrics by plan.      semantic_model:       enabled: true      agg_time_dimension: event_date      columns:        - name: event_date         description: Date of the signup aggregation.         granularity: day         dimension:           type: time        - name: plan         description: Subscription plan associated with the signup.         dimension:           type: categorical      metrics:        - name: signups         description: Total signups.         type: simple         agg: sum         expr: signups        - name: signup_revenue_usd         description: Revenue attributed to signups in USD.         type: simple         agg: sum         expr: revenue_usd    - name: fct_retention     meta:       physical_relation: user_metrics.retention     description: >       User retention by signup cohort and number of days since signup.      semantic_model:       enabled: true      agg_time_dimension: cohort_date      columns:        - name: cohort_date         description: Signup cohort date.         granularity: day         dimension:           type: time        - name: day_number         description: Number of days since signup.         dimension:           type: categorical      metrics:        - name: retained_users         description: Number of retained users for the cohort and retention day.         type: simple         agg: sum         expr: retained        - name: cohort_size         description: Number of users in the signup cohort.         type: simple         agg: max         expr: cohort_size
